entities.summary: The Duchy of Salzburg was a Cisleithanian crown land of the Austrian Empire and Austria-Hungary from 1849 to 1918. Its capital was Salzburg, while other towns in the duchy included Zell am See and Gastein. Before becoming a crown land, Salzburg went through numerous changes of rulership. It is differentiated from its predecessor, the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg, as it was mediatized in 1803 through the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss and remained henceforth under secular rule as the Electorate of Salzburg; in the following 43 years, it would undergo three more changes of rulership before becoming the crown land of Salzburg.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Duchy of Salzburg played a regional role in Austrian-Hungarian politics from 1849 to 1918, with its capital city Salzburg serving as a cultural and economic center. Its existence had limited but notable consequences for the region.
